skill.name: Plan
skill.prompt:
## Plan

Produce a complete, concise implementation plan for the current Goal Round. Choose the planning method appropriate to the work. For behavior changes, identify the underlying cause, governing concept or invariant, and existing owner before listing edits. Prefer strengthening an existing concept; introduce one only when it clarifies the behavior and reduces special cases. Do not change repository files. 

### Guidance

- Thrashing is a real danger with AI agents. To mitigate this, consider if the Goal is merely a symptom of a missing or misused concept in the target app architecture. Feel free to explore other Goals to determine if they have additional insights into this question.
- Over- or under-specificity can also cause undesirable implementation outcomes. Ensure that the plan has the information it needs for effective implementation, but not unnecessary details.
- Always use plain language.

### Format

Return an actionable plan with stable checklist IDs and meaningful verification.

Example:
Task #1 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
Task #2 - short description of the work (what) and the rationale (why)
(etc.)

### Intent and architecture

Review Refine's relevant documentation files under Refine's runtime at `<refine-runtime>/docs/intent/***/*.*` as the durable product specification.

default-plan.summary:
Plan: verify and complete the retained implementation. The worktree is clean at 0a85e69c, which includes implementation f3945f54 and the committed Skill-launch helper correction. No repository files were changed during planning; tests were not run.

Cause and governing concept: Controls combined operating settings with independently useful Skills and Sites entry points. Navigation belongs to the shared browser shell; Skill execution and Knowledge Hub management retain their existing owners. Strengthen that separation without introducing new APIs or duplicate editors. The runtime intent documents describe the earlier Controls layout; this Goal authorizes the new arrangement, already reflected in the retained worktree documentation.

Task #1 - Confirm retained scope. Review f3945f54 and 0a85e69c against their immediate pre-implementation base, 9c1be94c, so intervening main-branch work is not mistaken for this Goal's changes. Preserve completed work and correct only demonstrated gaps.

Task #2 - Verify shell layout and interaction. In index.html, css/base.css, and js/common.js, confirm right-aligned order Skills, Sites, Settings, New Goal; remove duplicate Skills/Sites sections from Settings. Reuse shared summaries, icons, rows, separators, panels, and spacing. Preserve Node/Reporter selectors and existing Settings and creation actions. Confirm mutual exclusion, action/outside-click dismissal, Escape, and keyboard focus behavior.

Task #3 - Verify existing feature ownership. In settings_skills.js and knowledge-hub.js, retain enabled Custom Skills for the active node and attached-app Sites. Each list must have a separator followed by its New and Manage actions, including empty/error states. Reuse existing creation modals, typed Skill preflight and agent-tab launch, management routes, and published/draft Site URLs. Confirm opening, definition changes, and node changes refresh lists while stale responses cannot replace current entries.

Task #4 - Check language and durable intent. Verify the retained navigation, Skills, Knowledge Hub, toolbar, Guide, and onboarding updates consistently describe Settings and the new entry points. Correct obsolete user-facing Controls references without renaming unrelated internal identifiers.

Task #5 - Verify observable behavior. Run the existing topbar, Knowledge Hub, screen-render, Node navigation, and Skill-terminal browser coverage with Chromium available; skipped tests are not passes. Run the focused Rust static-surface navigation checks. Confirm both themes, narrow/desktop widths, long-list scrolling, reachable action groups, keyboard operation, creation/management destinations, and both draft and published Site opening. Add coverage only for meaningful uncovered behavior.

Task #6 - Resolve the Quality evidence gap. Recover the exact identities and diagnostics of the reported 12 Rust failures and reproduce them against the retained candidate and 9c1be94c using the same environment. Fix regressions caused by this change in their existing owners; document verified baseline failures separately and retain unresolved findings for Quality. Do not weaken tests or infer a complete pass from navigation-only results.
